q: The nurse has attended a conference on legal and ethical issues in nursing practice. Which of the following statements by the nurse would indicate a correct understanding of the conference?
o: “A durable power of attorney for health care’s (DPAHCs) authority goes into effect once a client can no longer make decisions.”
“Advanced directives are routinely suspended during treatments and surgical procedures.”
“A ‘do not resuscitate’ (DNR) order must be renewed every 48 hours by the client’s health care proxy.”
“A nurse should serve as a witness to the signature of a client who signs an advanced directive.”

key.why: A Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (DPAHC) becomes effective when the client is unable to make their own medical decisions.

q: The nurse is triaging children in a pediatric asthma clinic. The nurse should ask the primary health care provider (PHCP) to first see the child who is
o: 14 years old, has moderate persistent asthma, and whose peak flow rates have dropped from 96% to 88% of the personal best.
12 years old, has mild persistent asthma, and has been using the prescribed rescue inhaler every two hours without relief.
7 years old, has exercise-induced asthma, and required the use of an albuterol inhaler while playing soccer two hours ago.
6 years old, has intermittent asthma, and awoke this morning with a fever and a productive cough.

key.why: Using a rescue inhaler every two hours without relief indicates worsening symptoms and possible status asthmaticus.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has had a C7 spinal cord injury. The client’s blood pressure has changed from 136/84 mm Hg to 156/96 mm Hg and the client is reporting nasal stuffiness and a severe, throbbing headache. Which action should the nurse take first?
o: Auscultate the client’s breath sounds.
Assess the client’s oxygen saturation level.
Elevate the head of the client’s bed.
Determine the client’s pulse pressure.

key.why: This is likely autonomic dysreflexia. Elevating the head of the bed reduces blood pressure and prevents complications.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has cirrhosis of the liver with portal hypertension and esophageal varices. It would be necessary for the nurse to immediately notify the primary health care provider (PHCP) if a client has
o: a musty odor to the breath.
an elevated serum ammonia level.
passed a black, tarry stool.
palms that are warm and erythematous.

key.why: Black, tarry stools suggest GI bleeding from esophageal varices, which is life-threatening.

q: The nurse has been made aware of the following client situations. It would be necessary for the nurse to immediately notify the primary health care provider (PHCP) if a client has
o: congestive heart failure (CHF), received digoxin two hours ago, and has a pulse rate that has increased from 72 to 83 over the past hour.
emphysema and has an oxygen saturation level that has decreased from 93% to 87% after ambulating in the hallway.
pericarditis and has jugular veins that are now visible when the head of the client’s bed is at 60 degrees.
has a suspected myocardial infarction (MI), is receiving a continuous heparin infusion, and has an international normalized ratio (INR) that is three times the control value.

key.why: Jugular vein distention in pericarditis can suggest cardiac tamponade, which is an emergency.

q: The nurse working in an emergency department (ED) is participating in an external disaster drill. The nurse should first assess the client who is
o: 8 months old, has a laceration over the left eye, a blood pressure of 84/50 mm Hg, and a pulse rate of 105.
28 years old, has a hematoma on the forehead, a Glasgow coma scale (GCS) score of 13, and is crying.
20 years old, has a traumatic left below the knee amputation (BKA), a blood pressure of 70/46 mm Hg, and a pulse rate of 124.
6 years old, has crush injuries to both legs, fixed and dilated pupils, and an absent pulse.

key.why: The adult with BKA and hypotension is in shock and needs immediate assessment/intervention.

q: The nurse is caring for assigned clients. The nurse should recommend to the primary health care provider (PHCP) that a referral be initiated to a mental health professional for which of the following clients?
o: 44-year-old who has multiple sclerosis (MS), and is reporting extreme fatigue and periods of forgetfulness.
39-year-old who has myasthenia gravis, cries frequently, and has developed a decreased appetite.
53-year-old who recently had a cerebral vascular accident (CVA), has labile emotions, and is uncharacteristically using profanity.
69-year-old who has Parkinson’s syndrome, a flat affect, and monotone speech.

key.why: Crying, appetite loss, and myasthenia gravis may indicate depression requiring mental health support.

q: The nurse working the emergency department (ED) is assessing a client involved in a motor vehicle accident (MVA) and notes a large hematoma on the client’s right flank. Which action should the nurse take first?
o: Obtain a urine specimen from the client.
Determine the client’s vital signs.
Palpate the client’s bladder.
Auscultate the client’s bowel sounds.

key.why: Vital signs give an immediate indication of internal bleeding or shock, especially with flank trauma.

q: The nurse is participating in the development of a staff education program about ethical responsibilities in nursing practice. Which of the following should the nurse include as an ethical dilemma that requires follow up by a nurse?
o: A family member is talking with the client about the client’s diagnosis while the roommate is present.
A nurse is preparing to administer a unit of prescribed packed red blood cells (PRBCs) to a client who is a Jehovah’s Witness.
A primary health care provider (PHCP) is placing a percutaneous intravenous central catheter (PICC) line into a client who wishes to receive palliative care.
A client who is scheduled for surgery in one hour does not have a signed surgical consent form in the medical record.

key.why: Administering PRBCs to a Jehovah’s Witness violates their religious beliefs and requires an ethical follow-up.

q: The nurse has provided discharge instructions to a mother who gave birth to a healthy, full-term male. Which of the following statements by the mother would indicate a correct understanding of the instructions?
o: “I should expect that my baby’s umbilical cord will fall off within the first week of life.”
“I should place my baby on his back to sleep for the first year of life.”
“I should wash my baby’s penis with soap and water until the circumcision is healed.”
“I should make sure that the bumper pads in my baby’s crib are hypoallergenic.”

key.why: The safest sleeping position to prevent SIDS is on the back until 1 year of age.

q: The nurse has attended a staff development conference on providing safe care for clients who have had a stroke. It would indicate the need for additional instruction if the nurse states
o: “I should assess the blink reflex of a client who has had a stroke.”
“I will instruct caregivers to approach a client with unilateral neglect on the unaffected side.”
“I will place the wheelchair on the client’s affected side when transferring the client from the bed to the wheelchair.”
“I should ensure that client’s who have a stroke wear their hearing aid and glasses while awake.”

key.why: The wheelchair should be placed on the unaffected side to promote safety during transfers.

q: The nurse is discussing the use of physical restraints with a licensed practical/vocational nurse (LPN/VN). It would require follow up by the nurse if the LPN/VN states
o: “I will release the restraint and perform range-of-motion (ROM) exercises every two hours.”
“I will use hand mitts rather than wrist restraints whenever possible.”
“I will make sure that I can not fit my finger between the restraint and the client’s extremity.”
“I will check on the client once every 30 to 60 minutes.”

key.why: Restraints should allow room for fingers to slip underneath—tight restraints risk circulation issues.

q: The nurse working in the emergency department (ED) is triaging recently admitting clients. Which of the following actions would be appropriate for the nurse to take?
o: Triaging a client who has a rectal temperature of 87.8^(○ )F and is bradycardic as urgent.
Placing a client who has suspected Haemophilus influenzae on droplet precautions.
Triaging a client who has multiple fractures as emergent.
Placing a client who has suspected inhalation anthrax on airborne precautions.

key.why: Suspected Haemophilus influenzae requires droplet precautions.

q: The nursing supervisor is participating in a disaster drill. In order to increase the availability of beds, which of the clients should the nursing supervisor recommend for discharge from the hospital?
o: 14-year-old with anorexia nervosa whose weight is within the fifth percentile and has a recent potassium level of 3.2 mEq/L.
2-year-old child who was recently diagnosed with cystic fibrosis (CF) who requires percussion and postural drainage twice a day.
10-year-old who was admitted with Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) two days ago and is receiving IV immunoglobulin (IVIG).
7-year-old child who was admitted with acute glomerulonephritis (AGN) and has a blood pressure that ranges from 140/82 to 154/86 mm Hg.

key.why: Despite a low potassium level, this patient is the most stable and can be discharged to free up beds.

q: The charge nurse has been made aware of the following client situations. It would be necessary for an incident report to be completed if a
o: client who has Parkinson’s syndrome falls while being transferred from the bed to the chair.
nurse who has not had the hepatitis B vaccine is caring for a client who has hepatitis B virus (HBV).
client who has methicillin resistant staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) refuses to take a prescribed antibiotic.
nurse documents the administration of a medication to a client one hour after it was given.

key.why: Late documentation of med administration can create legal issues and should be reported.

q: The nurse has been made aware of the following client situations. The nurse should first plan to see the client who has
o: cervical cancer, is receiving internal radiation therapy, and is attempting to ambulate to the bathroom.
thrombocytopenia and has a visitor who has brought fresh fruit and flowers into the client’s room.
bone marrow suppression who is receiving prescribed epoetin alfa and has a change in blood pressure from 140/94 mm Hg to 124/80 mm Hg over the past hour.
neutropenia and has a recent white blood cell (WBC) count of 3,000 mm³ and is eating homemade cookies brought in by a visitor.

key.why: The client with internal radiation must stay on bedrest to prevent dislodging the radioactive source.

q: The nurse in a community health center is screening clients for the risk of developing bladder cancer. Which of the following questions would be most important for the nurse to ask?
o: “Do you have a history of cigarette smoking? ”
“Do you routinely take non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)?”
“Have you ever been diagnosed with kidney stones?”
“Have you ever had more than two urinary tract infections (UTIs) in one year?”

key.why: Smoking is the most significant modifiable risk factor for bladder cancer.

q: The nurse is talking with the following female clients at a health fair. It would be most important for the nurse to suggest follow up with the primary health care provider (PHCP) for the client who is
o: 36 years old, reports taking oral contraceptives for the past 10 years and has not had a baseline mammogram performed.
57 years old, reports a 40-year history of smoking cigarettes and has bronchovesicular breath sounds ausculated between the scapulae.
67 years old, has never had children, and is experiencing episodes of vaginal bleeding.
48 years old, has been treated for an infection of the cervix with human papillomavirus (HPV) and has a negative pap smear.

key.why: Vaginal bleeding post-menopause is never normal and requires evaluation for possible endometrial cancer.

q: The nurse is providing discharge instructions to the parents of a newborn who was delivered vaginally without complications. Which of the following statements by a parent would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching?
o: “We should expect our infant to have a wet diaper at least six times a day.”
“We will need to bathe our infant in tepid water once a day until the umbilical cord falls off.”
“We will need to bring our infant in for the first follow up appointment at 2 weeks of age.”
“We should swaddle our infant in a blanket before placing our infant on the abdomen to go to sleep.”

key.why: Infants should have at least six wet diapers/day to ensure adequate hydration.

q: The nurse has instructed a client who was recently diagnosed with osteoporosis. Which of the following client statements would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching?
o: “I should walk for 30 minutes three to five times a week.”
“I need to swim for 30 minutes at least three times a week.”
“I will limit my caloric intake to 1500 calories per day.”
“I must avoid drinking grapefruit juice because I am taking calcium supplements.”

key.why: Weight-bearing exercise like walking strengthens bones and prevents progression of osteoporosis.

q: The nurse is preparing discharge plans for a client who requires treatment for infective endocarditis. The nurse should recognize that the factor that will have the greatest impact on discharge planning is the fact that the client
o: does not have an automobile or a driver’s license.
immigrated to the country from Liberia six months ago.
is homeless and intermittently lives in a shelter.
stopped going to school after the ninth grade.

key.why: Homelessness impacts discharge planning, medication adherence, and follow-up care for infective endocarditis.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who is receiving treatment for pancreatic cancer. Upon entering the client’s room, the nurse observes the client’s spouse sitting at the bedside, staring out the window, and crying. When approached by the nurse, the spouse states, “I’m so worried.” Which of the following statements would be therapeutic for the nurse to make?
o: “Are you able to take good care of yourself?”
“Life must seem very unfair right now.”
“I’ll stay here and sit with you awhile.”
“Have you considered attending a support group?”

key.why: This response shows empathy and therapeutic communication.

q: The nurse is admitting a client diagnosed with major depression. Which of the following questions would be a priority for the nurse to ask the client?
o: “Do you have a plan to hurt yourself?”
“How long have you been feeling this way?”
“Have you completed a no-harm contract?”
“Have you ever attempted to commit suicide in the past?”

key.why: Suicide assessment is always the priority when a client presents with depression.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has paranoid schizophrenia and a history of command hallucinations. The client is pacing and yelling in the day room, "I will do it. I will do it!" Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
o: Determine if the client plans to act upon the hallucination.
Ignore the client's behavior until the client becomes calm.
Using a firm, loud voice, instruct the client to stop yelling.
Encourage the client to return to the room.

key.why: Assess for suicidal or harmful intent if a client has command hallucinations.

q: The nurse is assessing a client who has borderline personally disorder (BPD). Which of the following findings is consistent with this diagnosis?
o: Ritualistic behavior to relieve stress.
Irresistible urge to cut self.
Binge eating.
Hearing voices.

key.why: Borderline Personality Disorder is associated with self-harm behaviors like cutting.

q: The nurse has instructed a client about how to care for a hearing aid. Which of the following client statements would require follow up by the nurse?
o: “I will keep extra batteries readily available.”
“I will adjust the hearing aid volume to the highest setting that allows me to hear.”
“I will clean the ear mold with mild soap and water.”
“I will turn off the hearing aid and remove the disposable battery when it is not in use.”

key.why: Setting the hearing aid to the highest volume may cause feedback or hearing damage; gradual adjustment is safer.

q: The nurse is instructing a client who has full weight bearing ambulation prescribed how to properly use a walker. Which of the following instructions should the nurse give the client?
o: “Use the chair arms for support when getting out of a chair to the walker.”
“Advance the walker 12 inches and then take a step forward.”
“Look down at your feet when moving them forward.”
“Hold the walker with the elbows locked.”

key.why: Support with chair arms prevents falls and promotes safety when standing.

q: The nurse preceptor is observing a newly-hired nurse provide postmortem care for a client. Which of the following actions by the nurse would require follow up by the preceptor?
o: Positioning the client with the head of bed (HOB) elevated at 60 degrees during family visitation.
Keeping the client’s dentures in place until the family has had an opportunity to visit.
Removing soiled dressings and replacing them with clean dressings.
Ensuring the death certificate has been signed by the primary health care provider (PHCP).

key.why: Elevating the head of bed that high postmortem may cause the client to appear unnatural and should be followed up.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has an ileal conduit. Which of the following actions should the nurse take when caring for the client?
o: Applying a skin protectant to a 2-inch radius around the stoma when changing the stoma appliance.
Placing a surgical mask on the client when changing the stoma appliance.
Notifying the primary health care provider (PHCP) if mucus is noted in the urine.
Instructing the client to empty the drainage bag once in the morning and once in the evening.

key.why: Applying protectant around the stoma helps prevent skin breakdown due to constant exposure to urine.

q: The nurse is providing instructions to a client who has a history of developing uric acid kidney stones. Which of the following information should the nurse give the client?
o: “Drink at least 750 mL of water every two hours. “
“Decrease your intake of foods containing purine.”
“Limit your sodium intake to 1000 mg/day.”
“Drink at least 8 ounces of cranberry juice every day.”

key.why: Uric acid stones are linked to purine metabolism; dietary purine intake should be decreased.

q: The nurse has provided medication instruction to a client with osteoporosis who has just been prescribed the bisphosphonate alendronate. Which of the following instructions should the nurse provide the client?
o: “You should take this medication at least one hour after you take your medication to treat gastric reflux.”
“You will need to stop taking this medication two weeks before having a dental implant.”
“You will need to sit upright for 30 to 60 minutes after taking this medication.”
“You should take this medication with foods containing calcium.”

key.why: Sitting upright prevents esophageal irritation and ulcers from alendronate.

q: The nurse working in the emergency department (ED) has received the following prescriptions for newly admitted clients. Which prescription should the nurse implement first?
o: Administer dexamethasone 12 mg IV to a client admitted with acute adrenal insufficiency.
Give lorazepam 2 mg, IM to a client who has alcohol dependence and is slightly agitated.
Administer human lispro 10 units SQ to a client who has type 2 diabetes mellitus and has a blood glucose level of 290 mg/dL.
Add potassium chloride (KCL) 40 mEq/L to the intravenous infusion of a client admitted with a suspected myocardial infarction (MI) who has has a serum potassium level of 3.5 mEq/L.

key.why: Acute adrenal insufficiency is life-threatening and should be treated immediately with corticosteroids.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has been prescribed dopamine at 6 mcg/kg/min. The nurse has on hand dopamine 400 mg/250 mL D5W. The client weighs 65 kg. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
o: Infuse the dopamine drip via an infusion pump at 14.6 mL/hr.
Monitor and record the client’s vital signs once every four hours.
Withhold the dopamine drip if the client’s systolic blood pressure is < 100 mm Hg.
Contact the primary health care provider (PHCP) for an order clarification.

key.why: 6 mcg/kg/min for a 65 kg patient = 390 mcg/min. With a 1.6 mg/mL solution, 390/1600 = 0.24375 mL/min = ~14.6 mL/hr.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who was admitted 24 hours ago and is receiving a prescribed continuous infusion of heparin sodium. It would indicate that the client is having a therapeutic response to the heparin if the client has
o: a decrease in the platelet count from 350,000 mm³ to 250,000 mm³
activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) that is 1.5 times the control value.
a decrease in the amount of petechiae over the chest and axilla.
an increase in the oxygen saturation from 88% to 94%.

key.why: Therapeutic aPTT for heparin is 1.5–2.5× control; this suggests therapeutic response.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who is in active labor and has received an epidural for pain relief 10 minutes ago. It would require immediate intervention by the nurse if the client
o: reports that she does not yet feel pain relief.
does not seem aware of the intensity of her contractions
states she feels tingling in her legs and feet.
reports the development of dizziness and lightheadedness.

key.why: Hypotension (dizziness, lightheadedness) is a complication of epidural and must be treated immediately.

q: The nurse working in the surgical center is performing a preoperative assessment for a 53-year-old female client who is scheduled to have a total hip replacement in one week. It would be a priority for the nurse to notify the surgeon if the client reports
o: the last menstrual period (LMP) was one year ago.
taking prescribed levothyroxine for the treatment of hypothyroidism.
taking the herbal preparations garlic, ginkgo biloba, and ginseng.
having a history of osteoarthritis.

key.why: Herbal supplements like garlic, ginkgo, and ginseng increase bleeding risk and should be discontinued before surgery.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who is taking a prescribed potassium-sparing diuretic. Which of the following medications, if ordered by the primary health care provider (PHCP), should the nurse question?
o: an angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor.
a statin.
a calcium channel blocker.
an anticoagulant.

key.why: Potassium-sparing diuretics + ACE inhibitors increase risk of hyperkalemia.

q: The nurse is teaching a client about insulin administration. Which of the following client statements would indicate the need for additional teaching?
o: “I need to gently massage the site after I inject the insulin.”
“I must mix insulin by drawing up regular insulin first, before drawing up NPH insulin in the same syringe.”
“I should not recap my insulin syringe before I dispose of the syringe.”
“I can keep the bottle of regular insulin that I am using at room temperature for up to 28 days.”

key.why: Massaging after insulin injection may increase absorption rate and risk of hypoglycemia.

q: The nurse is assessing a client who has a fractured left tibia and has a cast on the left leg. It would be a most important for the nurse to follow up if the client states
o: “Both of my feet seem slightly cool to me.”
“My leg pain has increased since I received my pain medication.”
“My cast seems loose around my ankle.”
“Can you do something to stop the itching I have under my cast?”

key.why: Increasing pain after pain medication could suggest compartment syndrome, a medical emergency.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has a sudden onset of slurred speech, confusion and unilateral weakness. Which diagnostic test for this client should the nurse question?
o: A 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG).
Lumbar puncture (LP).
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
Computed tomography (CT) scan.

key.why: LP should not be performed until hemorrhagic stroke has been ruled out (risk of brain herniation).

q: The nurse is reviewing the laboratory results of a male client who is scheduled to have a cardiac catheterization in one hour. Which of the following results should the nurse immediately report to the primary health care provider (PHCP)?
o: Platelet count of 85,000 mm³.
Blood glucose level of 162 mg/dL.
Hematocrit (Hct) level of 45%.
Cholesterol level of 235 mg/dL.

key.why: A platelet count <100,000 increases bleeding risk and should be reported prior to an invasive procedure.

q: The nurse working in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) is caring for a client who had abdominal surgery under general anesthesia. The client is receiving oxygen at 40% facemask and the respirations are shallow at a rate of 7 breaths/minute. Which of the following arterial blood gas (ABG) results are consistent with the client’s current respiratory assessment?
o: pH = 7.45; PaO₂ = 70 mm Hg; PaCO₂ = 38 mm Hg; HCO₃⁻ = 28 mEq/L; SaO₂ = 86%.
pH = 7.31; PaO₂ = 73 mm Hg; PaCO₂ = 51 mm Hg; HCO₃⁻ = 22 mEq/L; SaO₂ = 85%.
pH = 7.36; PaO₂ = 63 mm Hg; PaCO₂ = 42 mm Hg; HCO₃⁻ = 26 mEq/L; SaO₂ = 84%.
pH = 7.50; PaO₂ = 79 mm Hg; PaCO₂ = 35 mm Hg; HCO₃⁻ = 30 mEq/L; SaO₂ = 88%.

key.why: These ABG values indicate respiratory acidosis due to hypoventilation under anesthesia.

q: The nurse is auscultating the mitral valve. It would be correct technique if the nurse placed the stethoscope on the
o: fourth intercostal space, left sternal border.
fifth intercostal space, midclavicular line.
third intercostal space, left midclavicular line.
second intercostal space, right sternal border.

key.why: The mitral valve is best auscultated at the fifth intercostal space, midclavicular line.

q: The home health nurse is observing a client provide self-tracheostomy care. It would require follow up if the client
o: allows for two fingers to be placed between the tracheostomy ties and the neck.
cleans the stoma site with half-strength hydrogen peroxide followed by sterile saline
removes the old tracheostomy ties before applying the new ties.
rinses the inner cannula with sterile saline after washing it with half-strength hydrogen peroxide.

key.why: The old trach ties should remain in place until the new ones are secured to avoid accidental decannulation.

q: The nurse has attended a staff development conference about osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Which of the following statements, if made by the nurse, would indicate a correct understanding of arthritis?
o: “Osteoarthritis often occurs as a result of antibodies collecting in the joints from a previous infection.”
“RA presents with stiffness upon awakening which decreases as the day goes on.”
“RA primarily affects joints on one side of the body.”
“Osteoarthritis can be treated with immunosuppressive agents.”

key.why: RA stiffness decreases throughout the day; OA pain worsens with activity.

q: A nurse has just received report on a client who was transferred from the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) following femoral-popliteal bypass graft surgery. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
o: Teach the client to utilize an incentive spirometer every hour to improve lung expansion.
Determine when the client received the last dose of pain medication.
Assess the client’s dorsalis pedis pulse in the operative leg.
Assess the client’s boney prominences for the presence of skin breakdown.

key.why: Assessing perfusion of the operative leg is the top priority following bypass graft surgery.

q: The nurse is performing a preoperative assessment for a client who is scheduled to have surgery under general anesthesia. It would be a priority for the nurse to notify the surgeon if the client states
o: “I sometimes become so claustrophobic that I feel like I should run.”
“I had my will finalized last week, just in case something happens during my surgery today.”
“I have a brother who died unexpectedly during surgery when his temperature became very high.”
“I have heard about surgeons removing an incorrect limb during surgery, does that happen here?”

key.why: This may indicate a family history of malignant hyperthermia, a surgical emergency.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who had a transsphenoidal hypophysectomy 12 hours ago. It would require immediate follow up by the nurse if the client
o: has current vital signs that are T: 97.6 °F, P: 96, R: 20, and BP: 130/80 mm Hg.
has a 2 cm amount of dark-red drainage on the surgical dressing.
is alert to name and date but is unable to tell the nurse the name of the hospital.
has an intake of 1,000 mL and a urinary output of 2500 mL since surgery.

key.why: Excessive urinary output may indicate diabetes insipidus, a complication of pituitary surgery.

q: The nurse is caring for a newly admitted client who has a prescription for a continuous intravenous (IV) infusion of D5.45 NaCl with 20 mEq of KCl/L. The client does not have an IV in place and is right-handed. Which of the following actions would be appropriate for the nurse to take?
o: Prepare the insertion site with antibacterial soap and water.
Shave any hair that is located near the selected IV insertion site.
Insert the IV catheter in the right hand near the wrist.
Select a 20-gauge, 1 or 1-1/4-inch length peripheral catheter.

key.why: A 20-gauge, 1 to 1¼ inch catheter is appropriate for general IV fluids and KCl.

q: The nurse is assessing a client who has lung cancer and is at risk for developing superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS). Which of the following findings is consistent with this diagnosis?
o: Evidence of swelling of the arms and face.
A diastolic blood pressure greater than 100 mm Hg.
The development of petechiae on the chest and back.
A report of tingling of the lower extremities.

key.why: Swelling of the face and upper body is a classic sign of SVCS due to impaired venous return.
